Rejuvenate

/rih-JOO-vuh-nayt/ - the stress falls on JOO · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Rejuvenate means to make someone or something fresh and young again.

One afternoon thunderstorm rejuvenated the wilted garden, and by dusk every stem stood upright again.

Worked Example

The graying retriever had spent two years asleep under the porch, rising only for meals. Then the puppy arrived. Within a month the old dog was patrolling fences, inventing games with a stolen glove, wading into the creek he had ignored since his muzzle went white. The vet found nothing changed on paper. Everything else about him was five years younger.

Rejuvenate is the exact word for what the puppy did, because it means to make fresh, young, or energetic again — the years themselves seem to run backward. Revive is for bringing something back from the edge of stopping; rejuvenation starts from merely tired and old, and hands back youth.

How Rejuvenate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

revive

revive: bring back from the edge — a moment's rescue, not a handing-back of youth

renew

renew: make like new — said of things, supplies, and promises more than of people

Antonyms

drain

drain: empty the energy out of

age

age: carry it the other way — toward old

How Strong Is It? — refresh → invigorate → rejuvenate

refresh vs. rejuvenate

refresh vs. rejuvenate: Refresh is the small lift — a splash of cold water, a ten-minute break, energy topped up for an hour.

invigorate vs. rejuvenate

invigorate vs. rejuvenate: Invigorate goes further than refresh — real vigor poured in, a whole afternoon's worth — but it stops short of rejuvenate, which claims the years themselves roll back.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: again

Root — juven-

Root — juven-: young (Latin juvenis)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: to make or do

Put it together

Put it together: Re- (again) + juven- (young) + -ate = to make young again. Latin juvenis is the same 'young' inside juvenile; rejuvenate promises that freshness, energy, and spring come back — youth restored, not just fatigue removed. A textbook 'again.'

Use the root in a new word: juvenile

Use the root in a new word: juvenile: The juvenile shelf holds the books written for young readers — juven-, 'young,' labeling a whole section.

Word Choice

neutral / vivid

Rejuvenate claims more than refresh: not just energy topped up but years rolled back — said of people, spirits, skin, gardens, whole neighborhoods. Revive is for bringing something back from the edge; rejuvenate makes it young. In this unit's restore family, refurbish handles objects and recapitulate handles arguments; rejuvenate is the one that works on whatever is alive, or spoken of as if it were.
